questions.q: What does a database index let the query engine do?
options: Encrypt the field's values automatically
Find rows matching a condition without scanning every row in the table
Automatically create a custom field for reporting
Bypass all sharing rules for that field
questions.explain: An index is an ordered lookup structure that lets the engine jump to matching rows instead of reading every row in the object — the difference that matters most at LDV scale.

questions.q: Which of these fields is NOT automatically indexed by Salesforce on every object?
options: CreatedDate
OwnerId
Id
A plain custom text field with no special marking
questions.explain: An ordinary custom text field is not indexed automatically. Id, OwnerId, CreatedDate, SystemModstamp, RecordType, master-detail/lookup fields, and fields marked Unique or External ID are the ones indexed by default.

questions.q: How does an architect request an index on a custom field that isn't automatically indexed?
options: Open a case with Salesforce Customer Support — there is no self-service way to create a custom index
Check a box on the field's detail page in Setup
Add the field to a skinny table, which indexes it automatically
Mark the field as a formula field, which is indexed by default
questions.explain: Custom indexes are requested through a Salesforce Support case, including the relevant queries and approximate record volumes — there's no admin-facing setting to create one directly.

questions.q: What tool does Salesforce provide, in the Developer Console, to show which index (if any) the optimizer chose for an actual SOQL query?
options: The Schema Builder
The Object Manager's Indexed column view
The Query Plan tool
The Bulk API job monitor
questions.explain: The Query Plan tool shows, for a given SOQL query, which index the optimizer selected (if any) along with its estimated cost, which is distinct from simply checking the Indexed column on a field's own detail page.

questions.q: Why does having an index on a filtered field not guarantee the Force.com query optimizer will actually use it for a given query?
options: Because indexes on Salesforce expire automatically every 90 days

Because the optimizer only uses an index when the filter condition against that field is considered selective enough to meaningfully narrow the search — an unselective filter gets evaluated closer to a full scan even on an indexed field
Because only standard objects are allowed to use indexes at query time
Because indexes only apply to list views, never to SOQL or reports
questions.explain: Unlike many traditional databases, Salesforce's optimizer checks whether a filter is selective (matches a small enough fraction of rows) before deciding to use an index — an indexed field with an unselective filter condition still won't get the benefit of that index.
